chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to turn his face toward the people and say: 'O group of people! When the crescent of the month of Ramadan rises, the rebellious devils are shackled, the doors of the sky are opened, the doors of the Gardens are opened, the doors of Mercy are opened, and the doors of the Fire are closed, and supplication is answered.

And in it, God has, at every breaking of the fast, those whom He emancipates from the Fire; and a caller calls out every night: Is there one who petitions? Is there one who seeks forgiveness? O Allah, give every spender a replacement, and give every hoarder ruin!' — until when the crescent of Shawwal rises, the believers are proclaimed: 'Come to your rewards, for it is the Day of the Prize!'
Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Know that, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, it is not a prize of dinars or dirhams.'

key_terms.الْجَائِزَةُ: The Prize/Reward — the spiritual recompense given to believers at Eid al-Fitr, emphasized by the Imam to be spiritual not monetary
key_terms.تَلَفٌ: Ruin/destruction — the consequence for those who hoard and withhold from charity
key_terms.خَلَفٌ: Replacement/compensation — what God gives back to the charitable spender
key_terms.عُتَقَاءُ: Those emancipated/freed — believers whom God liberates from Hellfire at each iftar
key_terms.مَرَدَةُ الشَّيَاطِينِ: Rebellious/apostate devils — the most insolent among the shayateen who are specifically chained during Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual blessings of Ramadan according to Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) transmits a prophetic tradition in which the Prophet Muhammad used to address the people at the onset of Ramadan, describing its extraordinary spiritual blessings: the chaining of rebellious devils, opening of heavenly doors, acceptance of supplications, and daily emancipation of people from Hell. The Imam adds his own testimony — confirmed by a solemn oath — that the 'prize' awarded at Eid al-Fitr is a spiritual reward, not material wealth. This hadith was narrated in the context of encouraging believers to maximize their worship and charity during Ramadan, knowing that the spiritual economy of the month is unlike any other.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Husayn Bin Ulwam, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to turn by his<sup>saww</sup> face towards the people and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘O group of people! When the crescent of the Month of Ramazan emerges, the apostate devils are chained up, and the Doors of the sky are opened, and the Doors of the Gardens, and the Doors of the Mercy, and the Doors of the Fire are closed, and the supplication is Answered.

And in it, there is emancipation (libration) during each Fast. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Emancipates (liberates) them from the Fire, and a Caller Calls out during each night: ‘Is there one who would ask? Is there one who seeks Forgiveness? O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Give Replacement to every spender, and Give Ruination to every hoarder’, until the crescent of Shawwal emerges, he Calls out to the Believers: ‘Come to your Recompenses, for it is the day of Recompense!’
Then Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, by the One<sup>azwj</sup> in Whose Hand is my<sup>asws</sup> soul, it is not a Recompensing with the Dinars, nor with Dirhams’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ai-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from af-Husayn ibn ‘Uiwan from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir who has said the folio wing: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, would turn his face to people and say, “O people, when the crescent for the month of Ramadan appears, the devils of Satan are put in chains. The doors to the heavens, Paradise and mercy are opened. The doors to hellfire are closed and prayers are accepted. Allah on every first day after the month of Ramadan sets many people free from hellfire. Every night someone calls, ‘Is there anyone who asks for help or forgiveness? O Allah, grant good rewards to those, who give charity. Make those who do not give any charity to lose.’ It continues until the month of Shawwal begins, then the believers are called, ‘Come for your presents; it is the day of receiving rewards.’”
Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘I swear by the One in whose hands is my life, such presents are not dirhams and dinars.’”
